samples: This module loads a service's configuration from a JSON file and checks it as it loads. It requires a port from 1 to 65535, a worker count from 1 to 64, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, it fails with a specific error. You can instead use the fallback loader, which returns defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) or a configuration you supply. The older "load or default" function is deprecated in favor of that loader, and the module needs only read access to the filesystem.

This module loads a service's configuration from a JSON file and checks it as it loads. It requires a valid port (1–65535), 1–64 workers, and a log level of Quiet, Normal or Verbose. If loading fails, it reports either an unreadable file or a mismatched shape. It also offers a default configuration (port 8080, 4 workers, Normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply. Prefer that fallback loader, because the older load-or-default function is deprecated.

This module loads a service's configuration from a JSON file, checking that the port is a valid TCP port (1 to 65535), the worker count is between 1 and 64, and the log level is one of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape, loading fails with a specific error. If you want to keep running with defaults instead of failing, it also offers a fallback loader that takes a configuration of your choosing, plus a built-in default (port 8080, four workers, normal logging). An older "load or default" function is deprecated in favor of the fallback loader.

This module loads a service's JSON configuration file and checks it as it loads. A valid file gives a port from 1 to 65535, a worker count from 1 to 64, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. A failure reports either an unreadable file or a file that doesn't match that shape. It also supplies default settings, and `load_with_fallback` returns a configuration you choose when loading fails. Use that function rather than `load_or_default`, which is deprecated. It needs read access to the filesystem.

This module loads a service's configuration from a JSON file and checks it as it loads. It enforces a valid port number (1 to 65535), a worker count (1 to 64) and a log level (Quiet, Normal or Verbose). If the file is unreadable or doesn't match that shape, loading fails with a specific error. It also supplies a default configuration (port 8080, 4 workers, Normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you choose. The older fallback-to-defaults function is deprecated, so use the newer one.
